findings.evidence: `TauCeti.IsIndecomposableModule` is defined under `Semiring`/`AddCommMonoid` at `Indecomposable.lean:76-83`, while Mathlib defines `IsArtinian` under the same assumptions in `RingTheory/Artinian/Defs.lean:43`; the new proofs use only submodule lattice, disjointness, and well-foundedness operations.
findings.fix: State the lattice and Artinian results under `[Semiring A] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module A M]`, and place only the finite-length corollary in a separate ring/additive-group section.
findings.issue: The file-wide `[Ring A] [AddCommGroup M]` assumptions over-specialize every lattice and Artinian result, including `exists_finset_isIndecomposableModule_supIndep_sup_eq`, `exists_isInternal_isIndecomposableModule`, and `exists_isCompl_isIndecomposableModule`.

summary: The Artinian decomposition API is unnecessarily restricted to rings and additive groups, although its definitions and proof work for semirings and additive commutative monoids.
